Choose which `.ipk` to install, launch apps from the Updates tab, and test builds now show up as updates.

### Updates tab
- **Choose the package:** when a release has more than one `.ipk` (for example a standard build and a webOS 22+ build), adding the app asks which one to use. The choice is remembered, so later releases install the same kind of file.
- **Switch packages any time:** the app page lists every `.ipk` in the newest release with a readable name ("Standard", "webOS 22 and newer") and its size. Tap one to use it.
- **Skip the choice:** type a filter when adding an app and the package list is skipped. Both filter fields have a short guide to writing one.
- **Test builds count as updates:** the TV only keeps plain version numbers, so a `0.8.5-b2` build shows as `0.8.5`. The tab remembers which build it installed, and a test build of the same number counts as an update when it doesn't know.
- **Reinstall and Launch:** the install button reads Reinstall when the TV is up to date, and a new Launch button opens the app on the TV.
- **Clearer error:** a filter that matches no file now says so, instead of "No release with an .ipk file found".

### Downloads
- **Android:** `WebOS.Homebrew.Fork_1.0.3_universal.apk`
- **Windows:** `.msi` (x64 and x86)
- **Linux:** `.deb`, `.rpm` and `.AppImage` (amd64 and arm64)
- **macOS:** universal `.dmg` (not notarized: right-click the app and choose Open the first time)
